source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The ConfirmEx call keeps its nsString owners alive, names the positional arguments inline and explains nullable arguments beside the unsafe block. Its flags choose string titles for buttons0 and 2 and the built-in Cancel title for 1, so the unused button1 title is null. The checkbox message is null to omit the checkbox. When writing a safety explanation for this call, identify the owner, the flag that makes a value unused and how long each pointer remains valid. Pointer null guards alone do not establish validity. This is a scoped accepted-source example and writing suggestion, not an upstream API proof or a claim that all unsafe calls use this format. No native prompt or memory-safety test ran.
title: Explain nullable prompt arguments beside the unsafe call
